correctness.rationale: A two-set convex partition admits a separating line; symmetry forces all equal-area lines through the square center. For 0<=t<=1 the exact piece has four explicit vertices and four exact half-plane constraints. The maximal disk radius is forced by left/top/sloped supports and is attained with the right constraint verified. The diameter disk through (-1,-t) and (1,1) contains both other vertices, fixing the circumradius. Logarithmic differentiation has sign H(t)=4(1-t)-(t+sqrt(1+t^2))(1+t)^3, strictly decreasing with opposite endpoint signs, proving exactly one global maximizer and all square-symmetry equality cases. The included checker verifies polynomial identity and decimal approximations; the proof is independent of numerical sampling.

The inaccessible 2026 manuscript creates residual overlap risk, recorded explicitly rather than falsely declared absent.

value.rationale: Exact two-piece equal-area fatness of a square is a natural smallest finite benchmark for the 2026 equal-area fat-partition theorem and the fixed-number circularity tradeoff explicitly proposed by Damian and O’Rourke. The unique slope is interior, and neither obvious side-parallel nor diagonal cut is optimal. The complete exact constant and all equality directions are a nonroutine natural classification rather than an arbitrary computational slice.
